Germany dominated neighbor and historic rival the Netherlands in their Nations League quarterfinal match-up at Berlin's Olympic Stadium on Monday evening.

It was the team's sixth game under head coach Jürgen Klopp and the 50th ever between the two sides.

In a recent development, germany's 5-0 shellacking of the Oranje was their most lopsided victory since 1959, when they won 7-0. In all, Germany have now won 19 of those matches, the Netherlands have won 12, and 18 ended in a draw.

Sources indicate that speaking to German broadcaster ARD after the game, attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz — who scored twice in the fixture — said: "We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second half.".

Despite the loss, Xavi Hernandez's Dutch side will reach the final eight alongside Germany.

Prior to the match, Klopp had made it clear that he and his team were approaching Monday's showdown as a final after having lost to Greece 1-0 in his first home game in the job on September 27.

By night's end, Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck each scored once and Brajan Gruda scored once and added two assists on top of Wirtz's double.

Klopp has been high on Wirtz, who has come under fire for not delivering at Liverpool since his arrival there in June 2025, and his bet seems to be paying off with the 23-year-old now scoring four goals in his last four games for Germany.

In a recent development, "We don't care who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," mentioned Wirtz on Monday evening before adding: "We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team.".

A group of five EU member states, including Germany, have entered talks over a scheme to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda.

The proposal to set up so-called return hubs in a non-EU country had been revealed by the group — which also includes Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Denmark — had first been announced back in September.

Tesla has earmarked some €3 billion ($3.3 billion) to expand its factory in Germany, near to Berlin.

The Grünheide complex will be expanded to start producing the electric car company's driverless Cybercabs, with output expected to eventually reach 1 million units.

The Elon Musk-owned organization noted construction would begin in 2027, with the first Cybercabs rolling off the line in 2029.

"With this, we are laying the foundations for the world's most technologically advanced Tesla factory here in Grünheide," Tesla said.

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

Matt Pearson on our sports desk breaks down where the power struggle at the moment stands, with the deadline for candiates just a matter of hours away now.

Lawmakers in the state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania have voted in Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier.

The 52-year-old has been in the role since 2017 and is heading into a third term.

The vote was a secret ballot, but it can still be assumed who voted and how.

She received 39 of the 68 votes cast in the chamber, exactly as many as commanded by Schwesig's three-party coaliton of her Social Democrats (29), the ecologist Greens (5), and the socialist Left Party (5).

While Söder's comments in Munich focused in particular on the policy the coalition in Berlin had not delivered, Merz initiatlly focused on talking up the efficacy of his federal coalition.

"We are aware of the situation. We know that we now need to deliver. And we also know that we face difficult talks within the coalition. But I would also say from the experiences of the last weeks that there are solutions to the problems which we have in Germany," Merz noted.

Merz said that in the 18 months since last year's election, the coalition "has already successfully implemented many things, not 'set them into motion' as people like to say, but actually implemented.".

He noted a total of 17 bills going through the second and third reading process in the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, last week, "including the most comprehensive reforms of our intelligence and security services that we have ever done in [post-war] Germany.".

Among others, he thanked Bavarian Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, a senior member of the Bavarian CSU sister party to Merz's own conservative CDU, for his contribution to this.

Merz also touted the support given to CSU politician Ilse Aigner, not just from his CDU but from the Social Democrat coalition partners and the Greens, to become the next president, calling her a person who would "represent our country very well at home and abroad.".

After hailing these accomplishments, Merz then turned to electricity tax cuts, saying he anticipated talks on the matter on Tuesday that would be "very short.".

He noted that over the weekend, coalition leaders had revisited the figures, and now believed they would be able to "completely" reduce electricity taxes to the minimum European levels in 2027 "also for private households.".

Bavarian state premier Markus Söder has appeared with Friedrich Merz at a press conference during the chancellor's trip to Munich.

It seems Söder, Merz and the CDU/CSU believe they have unfinished business after the budget was finalized in the Bundestag late last week.

Merz had pledged in the run-up to the decision to provide a reduction in electricity tax for all, but the final agreement did not include this step, with the coalition partners the Social Democrats (SPD) saying it was not adequately costed.

Söder remarked he and Merz had discussed "backup for the coming days," for Berlin and for a "collective stance, that is really, really key.".

He remarked the coming days were about "demonstrating credibility in politics," seemingly in reference to Merz's promise that the coalition did not ultimately deliver.

Recent findings suggest that "That's why it's really vital to us that we do indeed bring about the reduction in electricity tax," Söder noted. "This is important for businesses. It would be a relief for citizens. But it's also a matter of credibility and it's written in the coalition agreement.".

Söder noted that as to the question of "where the money comes from, with a €560 billion (roughly $615 billion) budget, with €200 billion in new debt, nobody can tell me there's no potential within the budgeting process.".

A festive piece of merchandise on the right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) "fan shop" website has upset some religious leaders in Germany.

Called a "chocolate Nicholas," it appears to depict a semblance of Saint Nicholas in bishop's regalia and the party's colors and holding a book with "AfD" written on the cover where a Bible might be in more traditional iconography.

The Bishop of Essen, Franz-Josef Overbeck, was highly critical of the promotion in Monday's edition of the Bild newspaper.

Industry observers note that "The AfD is appropriating Christian symbols for party campaigning," Overbeck noted. "Showing the holy Nicholas in a blue coat with mitre, staff and the gospel with an AfD logo is not in order.".

Overbeck acknowledged that other organizations like football clubs would sell chocolate Christmas figurines in club colors, but he stated they would tend to refrain from including overtly Christian symbols when doing so.

Bild quoted an AfD spokesman as saying that as a "liberal-conservative party that clearly associates itself with Christian values," the item fit "particularly well" with the party image.

The main German protestant church group EKD's cultural representative, Johann Hinrich Claussen, noted the offer showed the AfD had "no understanding of traditions and no respect" for Christianity.

He described the action as "embarrassing and revealing," and stated that Christianity was "supra-partisan.".

According to recent reports, "The AfD knows little about what is holy to Christians. Otherwise, it would be aware that Bishop Nicholas of Myra, in what today is Demre in Turkey, stood clearly for uniting the occident and the orient. Beyond that, he is the patron saint of rescues at sea," Claussen mentioned.

The partner of deceased Bavarian politician Hubert Aiwanger has said that anybody is welcome at his funeral this coming Saturday.

Aiwanger was the economy minister in Bavaria's state government as the leader of the junior coalition partners to the center-right CSU.

"Hubert was a man of the people and so it stands to reason that anyone who liked or treaasured him is allowed to come to his funeral," Tanja Schweiger wrote on her Instagram profile overnight.

Industry observers note that she was posting after a requiem in the state capital Munich paying tribute to the leader of the Free Voters (Freie Wähler) party over the weekend. Around 1,100 people attended this ceremony.

Aiwanger died suddenly and unexpectedly on November 4 during a working visit to Berlin, aged 55.

Prosecutors have since said he died of natural causes, after he was found dead in his hotel room.

Germany's national men's football team will play neighbors and rivals the Netherlands for the 50th time on Monday night.

And there's quite a lot at stake for Jürgen Klopp's team in the last group stage game of the Nations League competition at Berlin's Olympiastadion.

If Germany win, they will qualify for the knockout stages, but a defeat could lead to potential relegation into the second tier of Nations League football.

Klopp was upbeat in the pre-match press conference at the prospect of playing the Netherlands, who he stated play "Xavi football," in the image of the skillful Spanish playmaker and World Cup winner coaching the team.

"I've always loved playing against teams like this. For all my coaching career," Klopp mentioned. "When someone says, 'hey they can really play football,' then in my mind the party's already started.".

Recent findings suggest that A full house with some 71,000 fans is expected in the capital when the game kicks off. Klopp played on the Dutch reputation for liberal use of bicylces in his comments to reporters, saying he wanted to "put a stick in their spokes" and dislodge them from the saddle.

Sources indicate that the notion of a bridge over the valley between Ratingen and Heiligenhaus to the east of Düsseldorf in western Germany as part of the A44 highway is more than half a century old. And the physical bridge itself has stood, complete, ever since 2022.

Yet still the crossing is not connected to any roads at either end.

A construction project to build the last 4.4 kilometers of highway and link the bridge to the A44 highway will formally start on Monday.

State premier Hendrik Wüst, as well as the regional transport and traffic ministers will attend the ground-breaking ceremony.

A project first conceived some 55 years ago has faced repeated delays because of lawsuits, environmental protection studies and onerous planning and permit procedures.

It has been revealed that the bridge across the Angerbachtal (Angerbach Valley) should improve the road connection between the North Rhine-Westphalia state capital of Düsseldorf, the Bergisches Land mountain range and the industrial cities in the Ruhr Valley. It's also meant to help remove some strain from the perenially busy A3 highway and to improve the road connections to Düsseldorf International Airport.

The last stretch of highway is expected to cost around €200 million (roughly $220 million), or roughly the annual costs incurred each year by forcing traffic to divert around it, according to estimates from Düsseldorf's IHK industry and trade association.

Construction is expected to take several years, no formal end date has yet been set.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz heads to Munich early on Monday, for a meeting with the leadership of the Bavarian Christian Social Democrats (CSU), the sister party to his conservative  Christian Democrats(CDU).

No concrete details about the talks were made public ahead of time, except for the CSU saying it would serve as a general exchange that had been planned for some time.

The trip comes a week after Merz nominated Ilse Aigner as the next German president, likely paving the way for her to become the first woman and first CSU politician to assume the role.

It also follows soon after the 2027 federal budget cleared a marathon meeting of the parliamentary budget committee in Berlin. This serves as one of the more conspicuous examples of the frictions and difficulties in the grand coalition between the Christian Democrats and the center-left Social Democrats — with the compromises it contains a point of frustration among the CSU and for state premier Markus Söder.

The northeastern state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania will likely vote in Social Democrat (SPD) Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier early in the afternoon.

The 52-year-old, who first stepped into the role in 2017, plans to lead a upcoming coalition of the SPD, the environmentalist Greens and the socialist Left Party after state elections in September.

The right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) emerged as the largest single party in the sparsely populated state.

But still, the political calculus that emerged was arguably simpler than in Berlin — where the socialist Left Party is the largest party but could struggle to lead a coaltion — and in Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD was by far the largest party but short of an outright majority.

Schwesig's SPD claimed 29 seats, with the Greens and the Left each taking 5, meaning that when combined, they hold a fairly clear majority over the AfD with its 32 seats.

According to recent reports, the SPD's relatively successful performance in the state, at least compared to its national struggles, has also led to Schwesig being linked with a possible return to federal politics. The SPD plans to elect a new leadership duo early next year.

Schwesig has already had a spell in Berlin as the federal minsiter for families, pensioners and women, and briefly led the SPD on an interim basis in 2017, but after this she returned to her home state to seek the top regional job instead.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, servus! Welcome to another Monday of news and analysis of matters making waves in German politics and society.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz is starting his week in Munich, at a meeting of the Bavarian CSU sister party to his conservative Christian Democrats (CDU).

In a recent development, this comes a few days after Merz naming CSU politician Ilse Aigner as candidate to be the next president, and days after the budget committee signed off on the federal government's spending prepares for 2027. Merz is expected to appear with state premier Markus Söder in a joint press conference later.

According to recent reports, far to the north, in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Social Democrat Manuela Schwesig should be voted in for another term as state premier in the regional parliament later in the day. Schwesig emerged in pole position after state elections a few weeks ago; some suspect her regional success could translate into national ambitions within the struggling party.

And in the west, regional leaders are headed to a road to nowhere — literally, but also hopefully not for very much longer now.

The vast highway A44 bridge over the valley between Helsinghausen and Ratingen-Ost has been planned for decades, and was completed in 2022, but work to actually connect it to the road network will only start today.

Stay with us for more on these stories and whatever else develops around Germany on November 16.

#128593. 73 goals from dropping deep - we ask Kane to break down how he did it

General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

73 goals from dropping deep - we ask Kane to break down how he did it

📅 04 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Harry Kane is one of the leading names in the race for this year's Ballon d'Or, having scored 73 goals last season for club and country.
  • As Harry Kane's career has progressed, the 33-year-old has taken an increasingly complete role, popping up to collect the ball as deep as his own box.
  • Many wonder why a talisman tasked with scoring doesn't spend more time closer to goal, but last season the England and Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals - the highest tally of his career - while playing deeper than he ever has done.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harry Kane is one of the leading names in the race for this year's Ballon d'Or, having scored 73 goals last season for club and country.

As Harry Kane's career has progressed, the 33-year-old has taken an increasingly complete role, popping up to collect the ball as deep as his own box.

Many wonder why a talisman tasked with scoring doesn't spend more time closer to goal, but last season the England and Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals - the highest tally of his career - while playing deeper than he ever has done.

When I mention this paradox, a grin spreads across his face.

"Until you really understand football and understand what we've been talking about, it's so easy to say 'stay high, you're going to score' but it doesn't work like that," Kane claims.

I sat down to speak to Kane about the finer details of his game, shedding light on his unique role.

Sources indicate that watching Kane train, his professionalism is palpable. England's record goalscorer is one of the first out on the pitch. The younger players indulge in playful kick-ups as he watches, engaged in conversation with a member of staff.

From a distance, that makes it easy to confuse him with a coach but, given his role on the pitch, it is a fitting mistake.

Kane's style of play reflects who he is as a person, with those who know him saying he is well-rounded and humble on and off the pitch.

How dropping deep helps Kane score.

The season is in its infancy but Kane isn't basking in the success of the past 12 months. With only five days of pre-season training under his belt, the England captain completed 90 minutes of Bayern's 2-1 win over Borussia Dortmund to lift the German Super Cup.

As demanding as his roaming role is, he has taken the physical demands of it in his stride. Across the past six seasons, STATSports - a sports technology firm Kane has invested in - found his distance covered, high-speed running and accelerations were up 8%, 22% and 42% respectively.

And given how the tactical landscape has changed over that time, it is particularly impressive Kane has been able to not only keep up, but stay ahead.

Kane's role has evolved drastically over the past nine years, with the striker now heavily involved in all phases of the game -Â including as deep as his own box.

"Over the last five or six years, man-to-man pressure has become bigger," Kane indicates.

"European football is physical and top teams are trying to win the ball back high, trusting their defenders and midfielders to defend man for man to win their battles.".

Given that change, the best teams have recruited physical athletes and brilliant dribblers who can beat their man when the game becomes a series of one-against-ones.

Kane, not known for his dribbling - and by his own admission "not the fastest", has thrived on his own terms.

Against Dortmund, there was a specific moment Kane dropped deep, looking to arrive in space unmarked. Recognising the danger, two players converged on the Englishman.

Kane's dribbling is cerebral. His speed of thought provides him solutions to problems others would attempt to solve with their feet alone.

Sources indicate that after getting low and using his strength to shrug centre-back Waldemar Anton off him, Kane rose, slightly adjusting his body to the right. These micro-adjustments are a hallmark of his game and through them he is able to shift an entire team's momentum.

Fooled by this feint, Daniel Svensson and Jobe Bellingham found themselves wrong-footed as Kane snapped the ball back the other way, opening up the entire pitch from within Bayern's half.

Kane wins his individual battle with Waldemar Anton, shielding the ball and showcasing strength.

As he rises, he positions his body to the right, facing his own goal.

Industry observers note that through clever body positioning, Kane moves the opposition towards the right side of the pitch. This is his cue to cut the ball back into the open space.

This allows Kane to evade two defenders, now facing the opposition's goal.

Earlier this year, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany shed light on Kane's unique role, explaining it as being 50% coached and 50% Kane deciding what to do.

Industry observers note that "I think it's partly instinct, using my football brain and getting the feeling on the pitch," notes Kane. "If, for example, I want to drop and see if the centre-back really wants to commit, he might commit into midfield, but is he going to commit if I drop all the way to my box?

"After the first five or 10 minutes you really get an understanding of how the opposition are going to play, which dictates how I play.".

Industry observers note that in the second minute of Bayern Munich's game against Arsenal, Kane dropped deep into a position normally occupied by centre-backs. Arsenal centre-back William Saliba marked him all the way, vacating space higher up the pitch.

There is a shared understanding at Bayern of an approach that allows team-mates to make sense of rotations that, to the naked eye, appear random.

Kane, who is given more freedom than most, is at the centre of it.

Industry observers note that "I feel like my position now is as one of two 10s, and you work together," he states. "You can double up on one side to overload, which causes the opposition centre-backs a problem of who to mark.

"If they want to mark both, they've got to go man-to-man and then that leaves space for our wingers or full-backs to run into.

"It's posing all these questions to the opposition but, personally, I love having someone close to me who I can link with.".

Kane built his reputation playing as a lone number nine, so it is interesting to hear him identify instead as a number 10 -Â in a front two.

"When you're the number nine on your own you can get marked by two centre-backs and you struggle to get touches on the ball," he says. "You're relying on everyone else to find you with the ball.".

Showing Kane two clips from last season, I ask him to talk through what was going through his head.

"The thing with our formation is, as long as there's someone in each position, it doesn't really matter who it is. Lucho [Luis Diaz] in this clip is playing as one of those 10s.

"I've come off to try and create a bit of space and Lucho's gone through the centre.".

Distracted by Kane's dropping-deep movement, one of the opposition midfielders is pulled towards him. This creates space, allowing Joshua Kimmich to punch the ball through to Diaz.

Industry observers note that "I think it's Serge [Gnabry] making the run in behind which takes the defenders back, which allows me and Lucho that space in between. Lucho lays it off and whenever I'm in that position, around 20-25 yards out, I'm always looking if I can get my shot off.".

It is one of many examples of Kane initially dropping deep before scoring.

"By playing deep when the play develops, I end up coming into a number 10 spot when everyone's dropped," he states. "I can get shots off from the edge of the box, which is a big strength of mine, or I'm running off the back of players where no-one's picking me up - because the midfielder finds it hard to [track].".

According to recent reports, the Frankfurt midfielder notices Kane dropping deep. Recognising this danger, he moves towards him.

With Frankfurt's central midfielder pulled towards Kane, Luis Diaz is able to receive a pass between the lines. He forms a central front two with Kane. The wingers ahead of them, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise, push the defensive line back.

Kane is found in space around the edge of the box and strikes the ball hard into the net.

The second clip is from Bayern's Champions League tie against Club Brugge.

Usually Kane is marked by an opposition centre-back, but the Belgian club give that responsibility to their holding midfielder -Â something he recognises and exploits.

Lennart Karl scores without Kane touching the ball, but the striker's involvement is undeniable.

Recent findings suggest that "These are the little runs, again, not everyone sees," Kane explains. "With Jamal Musiala and Lenny, they're so good at receiving the ball and dribbling so there'll be times where I will actually stay higher and let those guys get on the ball a bit deeper, and I'll try and make runs in behind.

"Without changing my game too much, I try and complement the players around me.

"I know Lenny is so good in those pockets and when he gets there, I'm more thinking of running in behind because, one, he can play me in and I can go through on goal, or two, he can dribble with the ball and do exactly what happened here.

"As soon as Lenny gets in that pocket I make the run and not always to get the ball, sometimes it is just to drag the defender away.

"Now he's one-against-one with a centre-back in the middle of the pitch and that's dangerous for any centre-back.".

Industry observers note that karl receives the ball in the middle of the pitch. As seen in yellow, Kane is being marked by Club Brugge's holding midfielder, rather than any of the central defenders.

Kane, recognising this, makes a diagonal run in behind, pulling the opposition holding midfielder away from the centre of the pitch.

Karl drives with the ball into the space created by Kane before putting the ball into the top corner.

With the Ballon d'Or announcement on the horizon, Kane's name is in the conversation, primarily for the sheer volume of goals he has scored. What is easier to miss in that debate is the rest of his game.

Kane plays for the team in each phase of the game across the entirety of the pitch, while at the same time producing extraordinary individual numbers that match the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland.

He has described himself as playing in the role of a number 10, nine and six at times.

In a football world of specific and heavily drilled tactical roles, that is quite the achievement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026.

Tuur Rommens has urged his Rangers team-mates to use a breakneck run of three home games in eight days to build a platform from which to launch a real assault on the Premiership title.

Derek McInnes’ side play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday and then have Falkirk and Dundee United visiting – with Belgian left-back Rommens clear on the need to use the Ibrox atmosphere as a weapon.

‘At the away games, there’s a lot of fans, but at home there’s even more, so it gives an extra boost,’ he noted.

‘I think, at home, we have to maintain our good run.

According to recent reports, ‘We’ll try to keep on winning these three games and then we’ll see from there. If you keep winning, you’ll be up there.

‘We’re back to Ibrox (on Tuesday) and it’s been a long time, but, yeah, it’s nice to play in front of our fans again.

Tuur Rommens (right) celebrates with match-winner Ryan Naderi at Fir Park.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed home the opener in Rangers' 2-1 victory at Motherwell.

‘I guess Aberdeen, it’s a difficult one, but we’ll try to keep on winning.’.

Rangers dug out a crucial 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday thanks to an 88th-minute Ryan Naderi winner and sit four points behind leaders Celtic with a game in hand.

Rommens believes the side’s ability to pull wins out of the fire and show they are willing to keep pushing right to the end of matches is helping build unity within the squad and with their followers.

In a recent development, ‘Yeah, exactly,’ he stated. ‘Also with the fans, when you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they’re so happy, we’re so happy, so it gives us extra boost to go on Tuesday again and try to get a win.

In a recent development, ‘I think the fanbase is unbelievable. It doesn’t feel like an away game because there are so many fans with us.

‘Especially for the fresh guys, that’s new. It’s the same for me. I’m not even here one year so I’m getting surprised every time that there are so many fans of Rangers when we’re playing outside.’.

Rommens also took time to lavish praise on Naderi and revealed what a deeply loved figure the Czech international has become within the dressing room.

Asked about the progress Naderi has made with his game in recent months, he replied: ‘It’s unbelievable.

‘You can always give the ball to him and he just keeps it.

In a recent development, ‘He’s very strong and I think he deserves all these goals that he gets. So yeah, I’m very happy for him.

‘He delivers, he scores a lot of goals, he gives assists, so everybody’s happy for him and he’s a good guy. Everybody loves him in the group.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that this Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

It has been revealed that looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

In a recent development, it could keep them at the top end of the table for a good while longer. They have already shown they can defeat Arsenal in a one-off match and they look to have the ingredients to stay the pace with them. In Fabian Hürzeler they have one of the brightest young coaches in the Premier League and he has a squad that are all on the same page.

Leicester upset the odds 10 years ago with a settled team, while this Brighton team has a deeper squad. When the substitutes came on in the second half, they slotted into a well-rehearsed system.

“We faced adversity. There was a little bit of luck but in the end they deserved it because they worked hard for it,” stated Hürzeler. “I want players who want to compete, to dominate. They all have the winning mentality inside of them. These kinds of performances are not about one or two players, everyone has to stick together.”.

Sources indicate that LOVE THIS TEAM SO MUCH! 🤩 https://t.co/QdBXsW1Ze5.

It has been revealed that hürzeler has played down a title challenge but his team have been among the most impressive in the first part of the season. The German coach, 33, has been in English football for two years but has learnt promptly the tried-and-tested response of taking each game as it comes. Next is Getafe in the Europa Conference League on Thursday.

In a recent development, while Hürzeler was reluctant to name individual performers, Dutch goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen was another key player in this win. He kept out Iliman Ndiaye and repelled Erling Haaland, who lost a physical battle with Lewis Dunk. “You’re going down with the Palace,” chanted the jubilant Brighton fans, with City now losing two Premier League games in a row.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday’s 3pm Premier League kick-offs.

The most eye-catching fixture sees Manchester City host Brighton & Hove Albion for the second time this week at the Etihad Stadium. On Wednesday evening in the League Cup, Enzo Maresca’s side squeezed past Fabian Hurzeler’s men on penalties (4-3) thanks to second-choice goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli’s heroics after drawing 2-2 in normal time.

Nevertheless, despite this disappointment and the 2-0 loss to Liverpool last weekend, Brighton sit third in the league, just five points behind table-toppers Man City, who suffered their first domestic defeat against Aston Villa seven days ago, which ended their perfect record in this season’s Premier League.

Speaking in his Friday press conference, Maresca noted: “I think we’re going in the right direction. I said in the last press conference, after so many years to change manager and many players it takes time to compete again and in this moment we are competing.

“We changed many players and the manager but good thing about the club is we are competing in all the competitions and we know it takes time when you make this many changes but in this moment, we continue in the same way.”.

According to recent reports, following a rocky start to the campaign, high-flying Bournemouth have won their previous five matches in all competitions without conceding, beating the likes of AC Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa by three-goal margins. Bournemouth host Leeds United as they aim to carry on this tremendous unbeaten run at the Vitality Stadium.

Elsewhere, Brentford are at home against Nottingham Forest, who have only tasted victory once in the Premier League and are winless in their latest four games, losing three of them, while the division’s two bottom sides, Coventry City and Sunderland, lock horns in the Midlands with both clubs plotting an ascent out of the relegation zone. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Going into the summer transfer window as Premier League champions, hope sprang eternal for Arsenal.
  • An opportunity to capitalise, encouraged by a sense at Emirates Stadium that their competitors were in transition because of managerial instability.
  • If ever there was a moment to strike in recruitment, this was it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Going into the summer transfer window as Premier League champions, hope sprang eternal for Arsenal.

An opportunity to capitalise, encouraged by a sense at Emirates Stadium that their competitors were in transition because of managerial instability.

If ever there was a moment to strike in recruitment, this was it.

The prepares were ambitious: a shortlist with more than 20 players on it. They were targets at Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid, even at Chelsea and Tottenham.

But as the window shut on Tuesday night, you could not escape the sense of unfulfillment - certainly from a section of supporters.

Arsenal's close season was one characterised by some unquestionable successes, but also riddled by difficulties and frustration.

Ahead of their home match against Chelsea on Sunday, BBC Sport details Arsenal's transfer window and whether manager Mikel Arteta, sporting director Andrea Berta and, perhaps most pertinently, owners Kroenke Sports Entertainment can deem their summer operation a success.

Bruno Guimaraes's Â£75m capture from Newcastle United was Arsenal's most eye-catching signing.

Heading into the summer, Arsenal were keeping abreast of Guimaraes' situation at Newcastle, although others were considered a higher priority.

For instance, their interest in Elliot Anderson was widely reported, but it was clear the England international was joining Manchester City.

Guimaraes' former Newcastle team-mate Sandro Tonali and Bournemouth's Alex Scott were also among the midfielders explored before a move for the South American accelerated.

At the ages of 26 and 23 respectively, Tonali and Scott are younger than Guimaraes, who turns 29 in November.

But numerous factors, including availability and price - Tonali joined Spurs for a minimum Â£92m - made their signings difficult.

Aston Villa's Amadou Onana was also among the options considered, but the Belgium international suffered a serious knee injury at the World Cup.

By mid-June Guimaraes, who had universal backing inside the Emirates, emerged as the club's primary focus.

Berta knew the player's camp well and Guimaraes was admired by Arteta, who had made it clear he wanted proven talent to take his starting XI - rather than the wider squad - to greater heights.

Berta used his strong relationship with Guimaraes' representatives to facilitate Arsenal's move, hence why Newcastle maintained they had had no direct contact from the London club until days before his move was completed.

It is not uncommon for Berta to lean on intermediaries to conduct negotiations, although the approach has had varying degrees of success.

For instance, Arsenal actively sought moves for Leicester City teenagers Jeremy Monga and Louis Page over the summer.

But sources insist that the lack of club-to-club discussions meant both players ultimately did not join Arsenal, with Monga eventually signing for Manchester City when he appeared to be on the verge of moving to the Emirates.

That said, Berta's success in pivoting the club towards a deal for Guimaraes when it became clear other targets were not viable was well received behind the scenes at Arsenal.

Industry observers note that the signing of Ezri Konsa was equally complex. Konsa was viewed internally as Arteta's first-choice defensive option.

Arteta wanted players used to the rigours of Premier League football - hence the moves for Guimaraes, Konsa and the failed efforts to land Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Recent findings suggest that konsa's ability to play at right-back was also viewed as a major benefit. Arsenal considered signing an orthodox right-back, with Ivan Fresneda among the options, but Konsa's versatility was a key factor.

But Berta appeared reluctant to meet Villa's valuation. A week before the Konsa deal was confirmed, Arsenal made a Â£40m offer, which was duly rejected.

Sources claim the deal was eventually sealed by the ownership at both clubs, and the transfer was agreed at Â£51m, with Â£4m in add-ons.

In the event of not reaching an agreement for Konsa, it is understood Tottenham duo Cristian Romero and Micky van der Ven were identified as targets â but Arsenal's north London rivals would not consider selling to them.

Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon is a player the club will continue to monitor, but clauses attached to his current contract make the deal difficult.

Tarik Muharemovic, who joined Leeds United, was another considered.

In attack, Christos Tzolis' impact since arriving from Club Brugge in a deal worth about Â£35m means the Greece international has been heralded as one of the discoveries of the summer.

It is understood the potential deal for the former Norwich winger was initially raised by an intermediary close to a senior member of the coaching staff during the close season.

Berta's number two, Maurizio Micheli, watched Tzolis play for his country against Sweden in June and was suitably impressed.

So far, the 24-year-old looks a positive addition to Arteta's squad.

Arsenal, who also made Piero Hincapie's loan deal permanent and signed Illan Meslier on a free transfer, are happy with the signings they have made.

The captures of Guimaraes and Konsa, who will both be 30 by the end of next season, have raised eyebrows given the combined Â£126m fee, amid concerns over how the pair's longevity may impact the natural evolution of the squad.

Yet it is undeniable that Guimares and Konsa add elite quality and experience to Arsenal ranks, and ultimately the club feel they paid the going rate to get those deals over the line.

Vinicius Jr signed a newly introduced six-year deal at Real Madrid in August.

While the club delivered proven talent for Arteta in defence and midfield, Berta's remit of adding an elite attacker ended in disappointment.

Rogers was the club's primary target heading into the window, and the early indications were positive amid a strongly held view internally that the forward wanted to join.

At the start of the summer, it was Arsenal's understanding that Villa valued Rogers at Â£100m. Arsenal valued Rogers at Â£80m.

Berta, however, was confident of negotiating the price down to a level he and the club believed could get the deal done.

In the meantime, however, Berta explored alternatives - Bradley Barcola, Kenan Yildiz, Yan Diomande and Nico Paz were admired.

Anthony Gordon was a long-term target, but he had agreed before the World Cup to join Barcelona.

Recent findings suggest that yildiz and Paz will continue to be realistic targets moving forward. Eli Junior Kroupi is another the club will watch once he returns from injury for Bournemouth.

Anderson's move from Forest to City for Â£116m, however, altered the complexion of Villa's outlook on Rogers' future.

Villa increased their valuation to Â£120m and ultimately Chelsea ended up signing the attacker for Â£117m.

Arsenal, it is understood, were given the opportunity to match Chelsea's offer but refused, believing their Â£80m valuation was fair - but it does beg the question of whether Rogers would be a Gunners player now if Berta had acted sooner.

Ultimately, the failure to land Rogers arrived as the first of a series of blows to Berta in his efforts to deliver a top-class left-sided attacker for the team.

Arsenal genuinely believed they had a realistic chance of signing Vinicius Jr before he decided to sign a newly introduced contract at Real Madrid.

Berta and Arteta were all in on the Brazil icon. The club were prepared finance the deal too.

While the transfer would likely have cost a British record fee and been one of the most lucrative remuneration packages in Premier League history, the benefit to Arteta's team and the Brazil superstar's commercial value meant Arsenal were absolutely prepared to complete the deal.

Yet well-placed sources expressed to BBC Sport over the summer that Vinicius did not want to leave Real, while others feared Arsenal were being used to strengthen the attacker's efforts to secure a more lucrative contract at the Bernabeu.

Those concerns came to fruition as Vinicius signed a upcoming long-term contract in Spain in another Arsenal disappointment.

There were similar reservations about Arsenal's well-documented pursuit of Julian Alvarez.

The Atletico Madrid forward indicated very little indication that he was willing to join Arsenal; his preference to join Barcelona was one of the worst-kept secrets of the window.

But Atletico's point-blank refusal to sell to Barcelona was deemed reason enough by Berta and Arteta to persist with their interest in the hope of Alvarez changing his mind until the closing days of the window.

Alvarez, however, preferred to stay at Atletico, even though his relationship with the club is at an all-time low.

It has been revealed that did Arsenal waste their time with Vinicius and Alvarez? The answer varies depending on who you speak to.

When it became clear Alvarez was unlikely, Berta explored his options.

Intriguingly, Arsenal have admired Chelsea striker Joao Pedro, who was deemed not for sale over the summer, although there were concerns over how he would fit into Arteta's system.

It is claimed Berta relies significantly on his vast network of agent connections rather than acting on the club's existing scouting information when analysing the market.

For example, last summer, when all the scouting information pointed towards a move for Benjamin Sesko, Berta's arrival meant the club pivoted to Viktor Gyokeres, who is at the moment second-choice striker.

This summer the club's late dalliance with Lyon winger Malick Fofana provided a further example of Berta leaning on his agency connections after management agency Roc Nation offered Arsenal an opportunity to sign the Belgium international.

Berta's relationship with Roc Nation was particularly prevalent this summer given Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius and the sale of Gabriel Martinelli, who are both clients of the agency.

It remains to be seen how much of an impact Arsenal's failure to sign a recognised top-level attacker impacts their season, particularly in light of Martinelli and Leandro Trossard's departures.

Arsenal headed into the window with a clear remit of ensuring the club become more sustainable and adept at trading.

Part of that directive is to ensure the club remain compliant with domestic and European financial regulations.

Depending on who you talk to, the size of the potential deals for Vinicius or Alvarez would have raised doubts over Arsenal's ability to stay within the regulations.

Nevertheless, ensuring they maximised the benefits of player trading will become an increasing part of Arsenal's financial operation in the future.

According to recent reports, there was already evidence of that through the sale of Martinelli, whose Â£60m exit to Al-Hilal was the club's record departure. Arsenal have also secured a sell-on clause in the deal.

The exits of Martinelli, Trossard, Gabriel Jesus, Christian Norgaard, Jakub Kiwior, Fabio Vieira and Karl Hein secured the club in the region of Â£114m.

Through intermediaries, a possible exit for Myles Lewis-Skelly was explored, with a fee of about Â£80m believed to have been mooted for the midfielder.

Manchester United, who were attracted to Lewis-Skelly's ability to play at left-back, were interested but ultimately deemed his valuation too high.

Of course, it is Berta's job to have a firm grasp on the level of interest in the club's players and their market value but, nevertheless, the thought of Lewis-Skelly's departure resulted in huge uproar from supporters.

As BBC Sport revealed last month, the Gunners resisted any temptation to sell Ethan Nwaneri on a permanent deal, the academy graduate landing a season-long loan deal to Borussia Dortmund that includes a January recall option if required.

The minimum Â£15m fee secured in Trossard's deal to Besiktas is also viewed as a good deal inside the Emirates given the Belgian turns 32 in December.

Having spent nearly Â£450m in 12 months, Berta's work in the market has helped the club deliver their first league title in 22 years.

Yet, despite the money splashed, there remain clear challenges in the squad - certainly in attack.

The summer window has left many supporters questioning Berta's body of work at Arsenal.

And with the average age of the squad increasing following the captures of Konsa and Guimaraes, can the current options build a dynasty of success before the club need to spend heavily again on regenerating the team?

Are Arsenal taking a risk in not signing a world-class forward?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Undergraduate students on university campuses played a significant part in spreading viral variants during the COVID-19 pandemic.Credit: Leonard Ortiz/Digital First Media/Orange County Register/Getty.
  • Universities have become hotbeds of SARS-CoV-2 transmission, according to a massive analysis of more than 85,000 viral genome sequences and other data collected from people with COVID-19.
  • COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Undergraduate students on university campuses played a significant part in spreading viral variants during the COVID-19 pandemic.Credit: Leonard Ortiz/Digital First Media/Orange County Register/Getty.

Universities have become hotbeds of SARS-CoV-2 transmission, according to a massive analysis of more than 85,000 viral genome sequences and other data collected from people with COVID-19.

COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.

COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.

It has been revealed that the study, published on 19 November in the journal Cell1, finds that viral transmission between 2021 and 2023 was highest in adolescents aged 15–18 in schools, undergraduates at university and residents in nursing facilities. Undergraduates, in particular, were consistently the first group to start spreading emerging genetic variants of SARS-CoV-2.

Surprisingly, however, staff members at all three types of institution had about the same risk of contracting COVID-19 as did those in their surrounding communities. So, for example, professors were about as likely to get COVID-19 from the coffee baristas in their university towns as they were to get it from a student at their university.

Recent findings suggest that the analysis is among the largest to bring together viral genomic sequences and medical data from people with COVID-19. “The scale is truly impressive,” says Bill Hanage, who studies the evolution of infectious diseases at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health in Boston, Massachusetts. “It’s an example of the depth and the detail of the picture that can be painted using the medium of population genomics.”.

It has been revealed that the findings were based on data collected from COVID-19 tests taken by people in Massachusetts between November 2021 and January 2023. The genomic data allowed researchers to trace the path of SARS-CoV-2 variants that emerged over time, and to link this with epidemiological data about the study participants, such as their age and whether they had been vaccinated against COVID-19.

COVID jabs for kids: they’re safe and they work — so why is uptake so patchy?

COVID jabs for kids: they’re safe and they work — so why is uptake so patchy?

It has been revealed that overall, the team found that booster vaccinations helped to reduce SARS-CoV-2 transmission. This was true even for BA.1, an Omicron variant that started to circulate in Massachusetts in late 2021 — a striking result because COVID-19 vaccines at that time hadn’t yet been updated to protect against BA.1, Hanage claims. “That’s an important illustration of how vaccines, even when they’re not perfect, can still be beneficial,” he says.

#128567. Trinity Rodman's non-negotiable for Washington Spirit: 'I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun'

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1852 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

Trinity Rodman's non-negotiable for Washington Spirit: 'I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun'

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1852 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that WASHINGTON, D.C.
  • Rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise.
  • LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized strategy is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it. Players and team staff scatter around a field and seem to bump into each other by coincidence, a sense of enthusiastic spontaneity coming over a wide variety of people. There was no actual shock in the fact that Trinity Rodman ran into Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang after their win over the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals last week. The sheer joy of reaching a third straight NWSL Championship, though, took over.

Rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise. The multimillionaire, clad in a chic gray cape that embodies a dignified but serious demeanor, then wasted no time clasping her hands with Rodman's and bouncing up and down. Sports team owners are hardly ever caught so candidly; no matter how much attention they do or do not attract, they are the resident corporate types, the odd ones out next to a bunch of athletes by design. For a moment on Saturday, though, Kang and Rodman were one and the same.

LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.

It was a perfect peek inside Rodman's orbit.

It has been revealed that rodman does not lack the seriousness that Kang exudes, her commitment to her craft just as evident as her skill. She is open to any and all questions about her job, whether they are very literally about soccer or about the nature of being the NWSL's brightest star, but not ones about aliens, which she made very clear in an interaction with a content creator on Thursday. There is a non-negotiable that's just as essential to Rodman's game as her clinical instincts in front of goal, one that is crucial to her appeal -- having fun.

"I just think you shouldn't be doing anything if you're not having fun," she stated Thursday, two days before playing in her fourth NWSL Championship with the Spirit. "I think I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun for me, so sometimes it is hard to show it and to experience it because you are so focused and there is a lot of pressure, but I'm hoping to always be that person that allows us to let loose.".

Industry observers note that five years after winning the NWSL Championship at the end of a Rookie of the Year campaign, Rodman is no stranger to the league's showpiece match. The Spirit are now the finalists for a third season in a row and are still in the midst of chasing their first title since 2021, but even amid the familiarity, this year is notably different from the last. This time last year, the Spirit's headliner was battling an injury in the run-up to the final and was in the middle of negotiating what would later become a historic contract in women's soccer. She carries none of that baggage this time around.

"I'm so excited," she said. "I think going into a championship is obviously always a blessing, but going into it not 100% isn't the greatest feeling because you know that you're still going to play, but you don't know if it's going to be a great performance, so I think to be healthy and to be able to give everything that I have is really exciting for me as an individual, but also to be able to contribute to the team and get these minutes in for the last hurrah.".

Rodman has played 32 times this season and averaged 86.6 minutes per game along the way, an upgrade from 2025's tally of 17 matches and an average of 56.8 minutes per game during an injury-riddled campaign. It has allowed the 24-year-old to set the tone on the pitch, as well as off it.

"She's bubbly and brings energy to the changing room," defender Esme Morgan said, speaking in the build-up to the game. "She always comes in on game day and kind of screams as she enters the changing room so you're like, 'Oh, Trin's arrived.'".

There's a playfulness to Rodman that is matched by the team as a whole, so much so that, on the drive to the team's training facility in Leesburg, Va., Morgan contemplates a list of questions that feels unique to the Spirit.

"I am excited to go in every day," Morgan stated. "I drive into training, and I'm looking forward to seeing the girls, and I'm thinking, 'What stupid conversation are we going to have today? What are we going to laugh about today? What silly thing are we going to do?'".

The list of silly things is endless.

It has been revealed that "We have these massive red gym balls in the gym, like exercise balls, and we enjoy kind of throwing them at each other, whacking them off each other so it can get very silly," Morgan stated. "I did accidentally knock [Gabrielle] Carle off one. She was bouncing on the gym ball, and I smashed one. I was aiming for a member of staff, actually. I kicked it and then missed him slightly, bounced off the wall, hit Gabby Carle, and she fell off her exercise balls, so it was funny. She was completely fine. No Gabby Carles were harmed, but that was funny, so yeah, we've been kind of going crazy with the exercise balls.".

Then there's Jose the Coyote, a plastic good-luck charm that is emblematic of Rodman's non-negotiable.

Sources indicate that "I think just finding little things to get excited about, if it's as simple as Jose the Coyote," Rodman mentioned. "Just latching onto little things that we can joke around about or have fun with, but honestly, we've been having a great time. We've been growing closer, and I think even just how many fresh players we've had join the roster, I think, has almost brought us closer because we do need to have more unity and language barrier and everything forces us to be closer, so I think the close-knit group allows us to have a lot more fun because we're comfortable.".

The joy is naturally rooted in something much deeper, if equally simple, after injuries have restricted her ability to focus on the task at hand.

"I think I'm just having fun in general," she noted, "because I'm playing so that's fun for me.".

Kang's interaction with Rodman at Audi Field last weekend is the type of thing that comes up in conversation unprompted, in large part because it is a snapshot of the Spirit as a club.

"Here are arguably the two people who have built us into this incredible organization with massive success," Spirit CEO Kim Stone mentioned. "It's because of the two of them. Trinity invests on the pitch. Michele invests in everything else ... [Rodman is] the only person who can jump up on Michele Kang and get her to dance and not get a different reaction from Michele.".

In a recent development, before Rodman officially signed a deal in January worth $2 million annually, there was no question that she was worth every penny. The player is "baked into" every layer of the club's business, per Stone -- season tickets, single-game tickets, jersey sales, viewership, you name it. She is the type of player the NWSL, with much hand-wringing and a new construct following a back-and-forth with the Players Association, built a whole new rule around. It is formally called the High Impact Player rule; in conversation, in headlines and on Wikipedia, it is known as the Rodman rule. A year ago, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman used her state of the league address to say the league would "fight" to keep Rodman around as part of a larger effort to sign and retain stars. Berman took her victory lap on Thursday ahead of another glittery NWSL Championship.

"Obviously, it was incredibly important for us to keep Trinity in this league," she stated. "The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field and we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her story and candidly, it's our job to continue to create more of those stories so that other people are just as excited about all of the stars that do play in the NWSL.".

Rodman, though, is singular in her value to the NWSL.

In a recent development, "She's baked into the fact that we get asked to play Denver [Summit] in front of 60,000 people, to play Bay FC at Oracle Park, to play [in] Newly introduced York for the Queens Classic," Stone noted. "If you look at all the milestone attendance, look who the opponent is. It's every time and so she's baked into all of that. I can't quantify that off the top of my head but what I can tell you is, when I worked with Miami Heat, we had LeBron James and then when I was at Golden State [Warriors], we had Steph Curry and those generational talents, what they do for your entire organization, especially when you have a good attitude and personality like Trinity, like Steph Curry, they transform your org.

It all comes down to Rodman's non-negotiable, something that will soon become a trademark as much as the goal contributions if it is not already.

"She's fun, she's engaging," Stone mentioned. "She's what people want to be around and they're drawn to and then she's phenomenal with fans ... If you have a personality, then we can help amplify what you're trying to do. If you are vanilla ice cream, I'm going to struggle to get a lot of people interested. If you're rocky road fudge sundae with caramel pecans on top, I got something to work with. I got some unique things. I got some fun stuff to do because what people want is just the authenticity.".

Recent findings suggest that rodman has earned the right to be the NWSL's transformational, singular talent, successfully receiving a torch that was left behind a few years ago by members of the 2019 Women's World Cup-winning U.S. team that captivated a nation.

Recent findings suggest that "Trin is a generational talent," Stone stated. "She transcends soccer. She is arguably the face of soccer in America, men's or women's, hard stop ... What you end up with is the most popular player in our league, the most sold jerseys in our league. The people used to shout for Alex Morgan. Now they're all shouting for Trinity.".

Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (861 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.
  • "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he said on Sunday.
  • But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for new candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.

"Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he said on Sunday.

But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for new candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football, people who aren't driven by financial interests," Klopp noted ahead of Germany's Nations League match against the Netherlands on Monday.

"If someone like that were to step up — if someone like that were to become president — I think that would be a significant improvement.".

According to recent reports, if that person is waiting in the wings, they're leaving it late to step on the stage. Despite a raft of federations and continental confederations, including Germany, UEFA (Europe), CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) and AFC (Asia), calling for Infantino's head in the wake of his proposal to sell off part of the World Cup earlier this year, the incumbent appears to have stopped the bleeding.

That plan, which involved forming a subsidiary arm of FIFA called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) in order to sell off part of its commercial operations to investors including Joshua Kushner — brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner — was widely panned before being abandoned.

It followed on from widespread criticism of Infantino's awarding of a new FIFA Peace Prize to Trump, the overturning of a red card for US national team player Folarin Balogun, and with Trump's involvement, at the World Cup and a host of other controversies.

Since then, though, many public critics have backtracked amid FIFA promising to release an extra $2.7bn (€2.45bn) from its reserves over the next four years to the federations, increasing their total investment to $6.35bn.

Perhaps the most significant of these u-turns came from the AFC, who went from saying Infantino had committed a "fundamental breach of trust" in August, to offering the Swiss its "full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a newly introduced mandate as the FIFA president" in October.

Those words were spoken by AFC President, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who ran against Infantino when he first won the top job at FIFA in 2016. He will not run again and said that "my feeling is, I'm sure, the feeling of most of my members," in regard to Infantino.

Proof that the sentiment is not universal comes in the shape of Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA). Tashima is one of only two people to confirm they will oppose Infantino in the March 2027 presidential elections.

The 68-year-old is a well respected figure in Asian football politics and will have no problem meeting the threshold of support from five of FIFA's 211 federations. This is not like the other candidate, former Swiss international player Ramon Vega, who is an enormous outsider. Tashima appears to be running on the basis that he will be able to chart a calmer path at FIFA.

According to recent reports, "I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association," Tashima told the Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon. "It's not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.".

But the numbers are against him. Though support from within the confederations may not be total, the backing of AFC and the African confederation (CAF) is a huge boost for Infantino, with those two alone making up 101 votes, almost enough for a majority.

Industry observers note that in fact, the only real concern remaining for Infantino remains UEFA. The European federation, headed by Aleksander Ceferin, is a major revenue source for FIFA but the two organizations are at loggerheads. As well as a war of words, UEFA are seeking to obtain evidence for a potential Swiss criminal case against Infantino in regards to FFE. FIFA have called this a "smear campaign" and a "fishing expedition".

But, so far, UEFA has not put up a candidate. Former Arsenal coach turned FIFA Chief of Global Football Development, Arsene Wenger was thought to be a contender but has now ruled himself out. Wenger's compatriot, Philippe Diallo, has since emerged as another option, with The Guardian reporting on Monday that the French Football Federation president could be confirmed on Tuesday.

It has been revealed that while Europe is football's powerbase, particularly from a club perspective, UEFA will need Diallo, or any candidate they can convince to run, to win votes from outside its 55 nations to have any chance of success, particularly with Tashima likely to split any challenge. Even if a candidate appears before the November 18 deadline, Klopp's hope for change appears to be a long shot.

Breaking: Rangers must find their shooting boots quicker to prevent the need to dig themselves out of needless holes

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1270 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.
  • He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.

Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.

That’s fair enough. He wants to keep the energy up. He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run. He wants to make more of the fact his team are capable of digging in and getting wins over the line by hook or by crook even when it isn’t going exactly to initiative.

It’s a form of motivation, and motivating people doesn’t always come through hammering on about their deficiencies. The truth is this, though: you really shouldn’t be needing a scrappy 88th-minute winner courtesy of a couple of jammy deflections in a game which has seen you deliver 29 shots on goal with 11 of those on target.

Yes, Motherwell keeper Alex Paulsen had a good night. One double save from substitute Findlay Curtis and Dujon Sterling in the 85th minute was quite exceptional. This, however, wasn’t quite the superhuman display from the Kiwi that many were making it out to be.

A lot of the saves he made were straightforward. Too often, Rangers blazed efforts high and wide. They dominated the first quarter of this game until Jake Girdwood-Reich cancelled out Manny Fernandez’s early opener, lost their rhythm a bit, as they are wont to do, and then ran the show completely in the second half.

They should have won by a country mile and it is necessary to look into why they didn’t.

Ryan Naderi rejoices in scoring Rangers' late winner against Motherwell.

Emmanuel Fernandez broke the deadlock on eight minutes at Fir Park.

McInnes was justified in being happy with many aspects of his side’s performance at Fir Park. Ryan Naderi did put in a strong display as he spearheaded the frontline, although he did miss two gilt-edged chances before settling it late on with an untidy effort that deflected off Martin Moormann — who had already blocked a Badredine Bouanani shot — and landed in the net.

The Czech international is developing a reputation for key goals that are getting Rangers out of the mire — and keeping them in contention for the title — but McInnes needs infinitely more in terms of numbers from those around him.

Not xG or pass completion or any of those niche interests. Goals and assists is what we’re talking about here. The stuff that really changes games and puts points on the board.

Industry observers note that first in the dock on this front, talented individuals that really need to be held to account, are attackers Minsu Kim and Bouanani. Listen, McInnes has already spoken plenty on the need for both of them to deliver more in those key metrics. He obviously doesn’t want to come across as a stuck record.

Sources indicate that both players are technically proficient. They are exciting. The view from this vantage point is that they very definitely do have it in them to be gamechangers, but they’re starting to get a little bit annoying now.

Thanks to the corner that set up Fernandez for the opening goal, Minsu, who started in a more central role with Kevin Kelsy being benched, does have one assist on the board finally. That’s a pretty grim return, though, from 15 appearances.

Recent findings suggest that particularly worrying from the South Korean was his reaction when presented with a golden opportunity to break his scoring duck just before the hour. Naderi teed him up perfectly with a pass to the left. Minsu had time to control the ball and pick his spot.

His sclaffed effort, easily saved by Paulsen at the near post, was atrocious. It reeked of a guy short of confidence in the final third and growing progressively more anxious about getting his name on the scoresheet. Maybe he’s just trying too hard, but he needs to get the finger out, keep the mind calm and start taking the heat off the likes of Naderi and Kelsy with some major contributions.

Sources indicate that same goes for Bouanani. His late effort did, at least, lead to Naderi’s winner, albeit more through accident than design, but his record reads one goal and one assist in 10 appearances. He’s a dangerous, tricky winger. He beats people for fun. He should be doing more than this.

Djeidi Gassama, a more limited player than Minsu or Bouanani, started against Motherwell and does have five assists to his name, but he’s only managed one goal, in a 5-1 League Cup rout of St Mirren.

Meanwhile, Findlay Curtis has no goals and no assists from 15 outings, although only five of those have been first-team starts.

According to recent reports, that’s four blokes who play along the frontline and they’ve managed two goals between them. You do the maths on that.

Derek McInnes was delighted at full-time but Rangers should have won with more comfort.

There are others throughout the team, though, who can be doing more to make life easier from a goalscoring perspective.

Sources indicate that fernandez unveiled himself as a real threat from set-pieces last season. He’s a real weapon in the air. Saturday’s goal was his first this term. Rangers need to do better at harnessing what he brings in an attacking context from dead-ball situations.

A few more in the way of goal interventions from midfield would be welcome, too. Dan Neil can finish. He showed that with those two spectacular goals against Celtic in the 3-0 Premier Sports Cup win at Ibrox in September.

In his 17 other outings outwith that match, however, he has only scored once and delivered one assist. He had a brilliant chance at Fir Park just after the interval and slid it wide of the far post.

Nico Raskin, meanwhile, has one goal and no assists to his name.

Industry observers note that he put one great chance from a header wide in the second half. Then he blazed over from a promising position after releasing Bouanani out wide with a super diagonal ball and running a ridiculous distance to latch onto the return.

Sources indicate that mcInnes insists he’s never seen a squad practise crossing and shooting like this one. However much they are doing in training at Auchenhowie, they need to bring it to matchdays.

In a recent development, everything is there for Rangers this season. There are definitely promising signs in their overall play while Celtic, of course, are poorly run from a footballing perspective with an OAP manager, and a fanbase in open revolt against the board.

Rangers now have a run of six games from eight at home that could — and should — be a real platform for a serious title bid.

They just have to wake up to the fact that depending on Naderi to drag them out of a hole and drag them over the line again and again and again is simply not a sustainable way of working.

Motherwell (4-2-3-1): PAULSEN 8.5; Sparrow 7, Girdwood-Reich 7, Moormann 7, Longelo 6; Fadinger 6, Priestman 6; Maswanhise 6, Said 5 (Charles-Cook 15 (Kanga 63)), Hodge 5 (Bjorgolfsson 86); Palmer-Houlden 5 (Hendry 63). Booked: Hendry. Manager: Alfred Johansson 6.

Industry observers note that rangers (4-2-3-1): Pandur 7; Sterling 7, Fernandez 7, Makhanya 6, Rommens 6; Raskin 7, Neil 6.5 (Chukwuani 86); Bouanani 7, Minsu 6.5 (Curtis 78), Gassama 6 (Kelsy 69); Naderi 7.5. Booked: Naderi. Manager: Derek McInnes 7.
